items.title: Is Consciousness Overrated? | Clément Vidal
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*Why would life be fundamental to the universe while consciousness is merely an evolutionary development?*

Clément Vidal explores a speculative vision of cosmic evolution in which intelligent life could eventually create new universes. In a rapid-fire conversation with Robert Lawrence Kuhn, he also discusses consciousness as a cognitive tool, a possible natural creator, the future of religion, artificial intelligence, and humanity's distant future.

0:00 Life and the Reproduction of Universes
2:47 Consciousness as an Evolutionary Tool
5:55 A Natural God and the Future of Religion
9:21 Process Ontology and Existence
11:46 Humanity's Distant Future

*Clément Vidal* is a philosopher with a background in logic and cognitive science, and co-director of the Evo Devo Universe community. His interdisciplinary work explores cosmology, astrobiology, complexity science, evolutionary theory, and the philosophy of science.

items.title: Why Physics Cannot Be a Theory of Everything | Thomas Nagel
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*What did modern science have to leave out in order to explain the physical world so successfully?*

Thomas Nagel argues that the very move that enabled modern physics to flourish excluded subjective experience, leaving consciousness as a fundamental problem for any complete conception of reality.

0:00 From Objective Reality to the Mind-Body Problem
5:17 The Irreducible Subjectivity of Consciousness
8:34 Why Physics Cannot Explain Everything

*Thomas Nagel* is an American philosopher and Professor of Philosophy and Law at New York University. His work focuses on philosophy of mind, ethics, and political philosophy, and he is especially known for his influential critique of reductionist accounts of consciousness.

items.title: The Great Filter May Still Be Ahead of Us | Robin Hanson
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*What if discovering alien life would actually be bad news for humanity?*

Robin Hanson argues that evidence of independently evolved life elsewhere would make part of our past look easier, placing more weight on the possibility that the Great Filter still lies ahead.

0:00 Alien Civilizations and the Fermi Paradox
1:23 Where Is the Great Filter
4:35 Why Finding Alien Life Could Be Bad News
6:17 The Grabby Aliens Model
7:36 One Civilization per Million Galaxies

*Robin Hanson* is an economist, author, and Associate Professor of Economics at George Mason University. His research focuses on prediction markets, signaling, and the future of humanity, and he is known for proposing the Great Filter hypothesis.
